open_points.subject: Unknown-reference refusal ownership and contract between `surface` and domain modules
open_points.text: "A request naming a record that does not exist ... is refused as State 0's unknown reference before that record's own checks" (A16 rule 1) and "It gives the \"unknown reference\" refusal" (State 3, Inspection/traces section).
open_points.question: Must `surface` pre-check existence for every referenced id before calling a module, or may modules detect missing records and return a typed not-found outcome that `surface` maps to the single unknown-reference refusal?
options: `surface` performs all existence checks up front per operation schema
Domain modules return a normalized not-found result; `surface` only maps it to the refusal
Mixed: some checks in `surface`, some in modules, with a required normalization contract
open_points.default_guess: Domain modules detect not-found and return one normalized not-found result; `surface` maps that to the single unknown-reference refusal.

open_points.subject: Execution-class computation used for agent masking
open_points.text: "computing an execution's class from the records it returns and the classes `bindings.read_binding` declares (A07 rule 5)" (State 3) vs "The class of an execution is the highest class among the values and files its NodeExecution or TrialExecution names ... it is computed from those records, not stored." (A07 rule 5).
open_points.question: When masking for agents, is execution class computed only from execution records, or may binding-declared output classes be included (and if so, for execution class itself or only for `failure_detail` class per A09 rule 7)?
options: Execution class strictly from NodeExecution/TrialExecution inputs/outputs only
Execution class includes binding-declared output classes for operation executions
Execution class from records only; `failure_detail` masking uses a separate class that may include binding outputs (A09 rule 7)
open_points.default_guess: Execution class from records only; apply binding-declared output classes only when masking `failure_detail` as a separate rule.

open_points.subject: `bindings.check_installed_instances` deterministic scope and first-failure ordering at start
open_points.text: "The start check that no credential header has the name of a required header ... is `bindings.check_installed_instances`, a required start step that `surface` calls right after `installation.load_installation` and before the store is opened" (State 3).
open_points.question: Across multiple services/instances, what exact iteration order and failure precedence must `check_installed_instances` use, and does this start step fail only on header-name collisions or also on manifest-read/shape problems encountered while obtaining `required_headers`?
options: Check only configured services with selected instances, in `service_id` code-point order; fail only on the header-collision rule
Check selected services in deterministic order; fail on any manifest-read/shape error needed to evaluate required headers
Do not read manifest globally at start; defer all manifest issues to proposal/send-time checks
open_points.default_guess: Check selected services in `service_id` code-point order and fail on the first condition needed by A09 rule 1, including manifest-read/shape errors that block evaluating required headers.
